issues.description: The Stock.findStockIngredient method signature is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement UML and the solution implementation define findStockIngredient(String) (single String parameter), but the template's Stock.java provides findStockIngredient(String, boolean). Moreover, other methods in the template (add, take) call findStockIngredient with a single String argument, which does not match the two-parameter signature, causing a compilation error and preventing students from following the specified design.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Stock.java to provide findStockIngredient(String name) matching the UML and solution. Either replace the two-parameter method with a single-parameter signature or add a single-parameter overload that delegates to the two-parameter method (e.g., findStockIngredient(String name) calls findStockIngredient(name, true)). Ensure add and take call the single-parameter method so the template compiles and matches the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement (and the solution) specify Stock.findStockIngredient(String) but the template Stock class exposes findStockIngredient(String, boolean). This signature mismatch can confuse students: exercise text and UML show a single-parameter method, and example usage in provided Main/comments expects findStockIngredient(String), yet the template does not provide that method, causing compilation or usage confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template to provide findStockIngredient(String name) matching the problem statement (either by changing the existing method signature to single-parameter or by adding an overload that delegates to the two-parameter version). This aligns template, problem statement, and solution and avoids student confusion.
